title: Registration, revalidation and indemnity
blurb: Know every revalidation requirement, the numbers behind them, and what to declare to the NMC and when.
question: A nurse is preparing to revalidate. She has 40 hours of CPD, all from online modules completed alone at home. Has she met the CPD requirement?

teach.body: Revalidation is the process every nurse and midwife in the UK, and every nursing associate in England, follows to stay on the NMC register. It happens every three years and asks you to show that you are keeping your knowledge and skills up to date and 'living' the Code. In plain English: it is a three-yearly check that you are still practising, learning and reflecting. The NMC is clear that it is not an assessment of your fitness to practise.

items.label: hours of CPD, at least 20 participatory
written reflective accounts on the NMC form

teach.caption: Plus a reflective discussion, a health and character declaration, an indemnity arrangement and confirmation.

head: Registration
Minimum hours in 3 years
teach.caption: Hours count when you rely on your registered skills: direct care, but also managing teams, teaching or running a service. Too few hours means a return to practice programme or Test of Competence before renewal.

teach.body: You need 35 hours of CPD relevant to your scope of practice, and at least 20 of them must be participatory: learning that involves interaction with one or more other professionals. It can be physical or virtual, so a live webinar workshop counts, but a module read alone does not. Each CPD record must show the method, the topic and its link to practice, the dates, the hours (including participatory hours), the most relevant part of the Code, and evidence.

steps.label: Reflect
steps.sub: 5 written accounts linked to the Code

teach.caption: If your confirmer is not on the NMC register, the reflective discussion must take place with a registrant before confirmation.

items: Five pieces of practice-related feedback: from patients, colleagues, managers, appraisals or team reports; written or verbal, formal or informal.
Five written reflective accounts on the NMC's approved form, each about CPD, feedback or an event, and how it relates to the Code.
Do not record anything that could identify a patient or another person.
Discuss your reflective accounts with another NMC registrant in a reflective discussion.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Staff Nurse Grace at a GP surgery
teach.body: Grace's renewal date is in four months. She has 1,200 hours, 36 hours of CPD (22 at a diabetes study day and a peer case review group, 14 from e-learning), seven patient comments and five reflections on the NMC form. Her practice manager, who is not a nurse, will confirm her. So Grace first has her reflective discussion with the senior practice nurse, an NMC registrant, then meets the practice manager for confirmation and submits online through MyNMC.

teach.h: Declaring cautions and charges: two different duties
teach.caption: Protected cautions and convictions do not need to be disclosed under Code 23.2.

teach.text: Do not wait for revalidation to declare a caution or charge. Code 23.2 says tell the NMC and your employers AS SOON AS YOU CAN. And remember: 20 PARTICIPATORY hours are part of the 35, not extra to them.

items: Every 3 years: 450 hours (900 for two registrations), 35 CPD hours with 20 participatory, 5 feedback, 5 reflections.
Reflective discussion with another NMC registrant, then confirmation; health and character declaration; indemnity.
Code 12.1: have an indemnity arrangement relevant to your scope of practice.
Code 23.2: report cautions and charges to the NMC and employers as soon as you can.

summary: You can now list every revalidation requirement with its numbers and explain participatory CPD, reflective discussion and confirmation. You also know what to declare to the NMC and that cautions and charges are reported straight away, not at renewal.

A.q: How often must a registered nurse in the UK revalidate with the NMC?
options: Every year
Every two years
Every three years
Every five years
A.why: The NMC asks nurses, midwives and nursing associates to revalidate every three years to maintain registration.

whyNot.0: Registration fees are annual, but revalidation is three-yearly.
whyNot.1: There is no two-yearly revalidation cycle for the NMC.
whyNot.3: Five years is longer than the NMC's three-year revalidation period.

A.q: A nurse holds a single registration. What is the minimum number of practice hours she needs for revalidation?
options: 450 hours in three years
900 hours in three years
450 hours in each year
750 hours in five years
A.why: The minimum is 450 practice hours over the three-year period for a single registration.

whyNot.1: 900 hours applies to two registrations, such as nurse and midwife.
whyNot.2: The 450 hours are over the whole three years, not every year.
whyNot.3: The NMC requirement is set over three years, not five.

A.q: Of the 35 hours of CPD needed for revalidation, how many must be participatory learning?
options: 10 hours
15 hours
35 hours
20 hours
A.why: At least 20 of the 35 CPD hours must include participatory learning, meaning interaction with one or more other professionals.

whyNot.0: 10 hours is below the NMC minimum of 20 participatory hours.
whyNot.1: 15 hours is below the NMC minimum of 20 participatory hours.
whyNot.2: Up to 15 of the 35 hours can be non-participatory.

B.q: Which activity counts as participatory CPD for revalidation?
options: Reading a journal article on wound care
Joining a live online workshop with other nurses
Completing a self-directed e-learning module
Watching a recorded lecture on medicines safety
B.why: Participatory learning involves interaction with one or more other professionals, in a physical or virtual setting, so a live online workshop counts.

whyNot.0: Reading alone involves no interaction with other professionals.
whyNot.2: Self-directed e-learning without interaction is non-participatory.
whyNot.3: A recorded lecture is watched without interacting with others.

B.q: A nurse's confirmer is her line manager, who is a physiotherapist. What must happen with her reflective discussion?
options: The physiotherapist can hold it as part of confirmation
It can be replaced by a sixth written reflective account
It is optional when the confirmer is not a nurse
It must be with an NMC registrant before confirmation
B.why: The reflective discussion must be with another NMC registrant. If the confirmer is not on the NMC register, the discussion must take place before confirmation.

whyNot.0: A physiotherapist is not an NMC registrant, so cannot hold the reflective discussion.
whyNot.1: No extra written account can replace the reflective discussion.
whyNot.2: The reflective discussion is a requirement for every registrant.

B.q: A nurse is charged with a criminal offence eight months before her revalidation date. What should she do?
options: Tell the NMC and her employer as soon as she can
Declare it on her revalidation application
Tell her employer and wait for the verdict
Tell the NMC if she is convicted of the offence
B.why: Code 23.2: tell both the NMC and any employers as soon as you can about any caution or charge against you.

whyNot.1: Waiting eight months for revalidation does not meet 'as soon as you can'.
whyNot.2: Both the NMC and employers must be told, and the charge itself must be reported.
whyNot.3: A charge must be reported, not just a conviction.

C.q: Joseph wants to use a patient's thank-you card as feedback. He plans to photocopy it, including the patient's name, into his portfolio. What is the best advice?
options: Copy it in full, as it is evidence for the confirmer
Leave it out, as patient feedback cannot be used
Note its content and use, with no identifying details
Ask the patient to sign consent for the copy
C.why: Feedback can come from patients, but registrants must not record information that could identify another person. Noting the content and how it improved practice is recommended.

whyNot.0: Keeping the patient's name in the portfolio breaches the NMC's non-identifiable information requirement.
whyNot.1: Patient feedback is an acceptable source of practice-related feedback.
whyNot.3: The NMC asks registrants not to record identifiable information in the first place.

C.q: A nurse has worked 300 hours in the last three years after a career break. Her renewal date is next month. What does the NMC require?
options: She can renew and make up the hours next cycle
Complete return to practice or a Test of Competence
Her confirmer can approve renewal on reduced hours
She can renew if she adds 150 hours of extra CPD
C.why: If you have not practised the required hours, you must complete an approved return to practice programme or a Test of Competence before renewal.

whyNot.0: Hours cannot be carried into the next cycle; the minimum applies now.
whyNot.2: Confirmers cannot waive the practice hours requirement.
whyNot.3: CPD is a separate requirement; extra CPD cannot make up missing practice hours, which need return to practice or a Test of Competence.

C.q: A nurse plans to start private aesthetic work at weekends. Which requirement must be in place before she starts?
options: A written reflective account on aesthetics
A second line manager to act as confirmer
Approval from her NHS employer's HR team
An indemnity arrangement covering that practice
C.why: Code 12.1: have an appropriate indemnity arrangement in place relevant to your scope of practice. NHS employer cover does not extend to private work.

whyNot.0: Reflective accounts relate to past practice for revalidation, not a condition of starting work.
whyNot.1: One confirmer is needed at revalidation; it is unrelated to starting new work.
whyNot.2: Employer HR approval is not the Code requirement for new practice.

reteach.title: Revalidation as a 3-year suitcase
reteach.question: What has to be packed in the suitcase before the NMC lets you through the gate?

blocks.body: Picture a suitcase you fill over three years: a log of practice hours, CPD certificates with notes, five feedback notes and five reflection forms. Near the end you open it with another nurse (reflective discussion), show it to your confirmer, then declare your health and character and indemnity at the gate (MyNMC).

blocks.text: Revalidation is NOT a fitness to practise assessment. It encourages reflection and public confidence; fitness to practise concerns are handled separately.

explain.body: 450 hours over three years for one registration, 900 for two. Hours count when you use your registered skills, including management and teaching.

test.q: A registered nurse who is also a registered midwife renews both registrations. How many practice hours does she need?
options: 900 hours
450 hours
675 hours
1,350 hours
test.why: Two registrations, such as nurse and midwife, need 900 hours: 450 for each.

whyNot.1: 450 hours is the minimum for one registration.

explain.body: 35 hours with at least 20 participatory. Record the method, topic and link to practice, dates, hours, relevant part of the Code and evidence.

test.q: Which item must a CPD record for revalidation include?
options: A certificate signed by a manager
A pass mark from an assessment
The part of the Code most relevant
The cost of the activity
test.why: The NMC requires the CPD record to identify the part of the Code most relevant to the activity, with the method, topic, dates, hours and evidence.

whyNot.0: Evidence is needed, but a manager's signature is not specified.
whyNot.1: No assessment or pass mark is required.
whyNot.3: Cost is not part of the NMC record.

explain.body: Five pieces of feedback from any source, with no identifiable details, and five reflective accounts on the approved form linked to the Code.

test.q: What must each of the five written reflective accounts be linked to?
options: A formal complaint
The Code
A clinical audit
A named patient
test.why: Each reflective account must refer to CPD, feedback or an event and how it relates to the Code.

whyNot.0: Complaints can prompt reflection, but they are not required.
whyNot.2: Audits are not a required link.

explain.body: Reflective discussion with another NMC registrant, then confirmation (usually your line manager), then health and character and indemnity declarations online.

test.q: Which must be declared in the health and character declaration at revalidation?
options: Any parking fines
Sickness absence days
Any change of employer
A formal police caution
test.why: Registrants must declare if they have been charged, convicted (including a conditional discharge) or issued with a formal caution.

whyNot.0: Parking fines are not criminal convictions requiring declaration.
whyNot.1: Sickness absence is not a declaration item.
whyNot.2: Changing employer is not a character declaration.
